# The topology bar's undo and redo never say how far they reach

`Serves:` **#18553** — this is that ticket's AC-1, which its own body marks *"Independently shippable, and should land first."* Splitting it replaces that scope rather than adding to it: AC-1 is struck through on #18553 and pointed here.

## Context

Raised by @tobiu against the Workstation topology bar — first as *"the undo and redo buttons should indicate how many steps there are"*, then, against a screenshot of the bar, *"undo and redo look a bit unstyled (ugly) => missing icon colors, and i really do not like the disabled state gray. for step counts => neo buttons do support badges."*

The depth half and the paint half arrived as two complaints. They are one lane because the same two controls carry both, and because the second is a prerequisite for the first: a badge on a control the app never finished styling inherits the platform's colours rather than the product's.

## The Problem

The controls say only whether they can be pressed. Enabled-ness cannot answer *"how far back does this go"*, so a user presses hopefully and finds out by pressing — on the one control whose whole purpose is to make an action reversible.

The paint half is a single omission with two visible symptoms. `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss` sets five `--button-*` tokens: background, background-hover, border, height, text-color. **No glyph token and no disabled token.** So the icons carry no themed colour, and the disabled state falls through to the platform.

## The Architectural Reality

⚠️ **Two of the three pieces are readouts of data and tokens that already exist. Nothing here needs a new publisher.**

**The depth is already published.** `Neo.manager.Transaction#historyState` emits `canUndo · canRedo · historyCursor · historyDepth · historyLength` to every window bound into the Group. `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs#createTopologyBar` currently binds **only** `disabled` off that same leaf. `cursor` starts at `-1` and `canUndo` is `cursor > -1`, so the steps behind the cursor are `cursor + 1`; `canRedo` is `cursor < count - 1`, so the steps ahead are `count - 1 - cursor`.

**The widget already exists.** `src/button/Base.mjs` ships `badgeText_` / `badgePosition_` rendering a `.neo-button-badge` node, and `afterSetBadgeText` sets `removeDom` from the value — so a `null` count removes the badge rather than painting a `0`.

**The engine documents the disabled half and assigns it to the consumer.** `resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss` keeps `color` inheriting at the button root so the child glyph and text nodes can own themed colours; its own comment records that projecting the native `disabled` attribute activates the UA `button:disabled` cascade and that Chromium paints `GrayText` into the gap. Every token needed already exists: `--button-glyph-color[-hover|-disabled]`, `--button-text-color-disabled`, `--button-background-color[-disabled]`, `--button-border-disabled`, `--button-opacity-disabled`, `--button-badge-background-color`, `--button-badge-color`. The grey is not an engine defect and must not be repaired there.

**One cascade trap sits in the way of the badge.** `.neo-toolbar` paints its padding from `--toolbar-padding`; `.workstation-topologybar` declares a plain `padding`, which loses to it at equal specificity on source order. The bar therefore runs at the shared 5px, it is flush against the window's right edge, and the trailing control's badge — offset `-10px` outward by `--button-badge-margin-left` — lands past the viewport.

## The Fix

1. Bind `badgeText` on both actions, from the already-published `historyCursor` / `historyLength`, through one shared helper so the two counts cannot drift into different notions of "available" and the missing-Group answer is decided once.
2. Name the glyph, disabled and badge tokens in the workstation's own scope, in both themes.
3. Route the bar's padding through `--toolbar-padding` so the declaration is live and the trailing badge has room.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1** Undo and redo expose the steps remaining in their own direction, bound from the already-published `historyCursor` / `historyLength`. **No mirrored state and no new publisher.**
- **AC-2** `historyDepth` is not used as the count. It is the Group's configured cap, not a live measure, and would read as a constant.
- **AC-3** A count of zero shows no badge at all, rather than a `0` on a control that is disabled for the same reason. A retired or unknown Group shows none either — the same fail-closed reading `disabled` already takes.
- **AC-4** ⚠️ **Both directions witnessed, in the state where they differ.** One step back and one step forward must be asserted together: swapped, mirrored and off-by-one formulas all read alike anywhere else, and a constant survives any single state.
- **AC-5** The controls carry themed glyph, text, background and border colours in **both** `theme-neo-dark` and `theme-neo-light`, in enabled, hover and disabled states. The disabled state is a colour change, not the UA `GrayText` and not an opacity wash over the label.
- **AC-6** The trailing control's badge is fully inside the viewport when the bar is flush right.

## Out of Scope

Everything else on #18553: the modified-from-default indicator, the reset, its confirmation, and what reset does to the persisted record. Undo/redo behaviour itself — this ticket only reads what the Group already publishes. Any change to `src/button/**` or `src/toolbar/**`: the tokens exist, and the missing paint is the consumer's.

## Avoided Traps

Do not mirror the depth onto the workspace. `createTopologyBar`'s own comment records why: `getData` resolves to the Group leaf's `core.Config` and re-runs on change, with *"no mirror to keep in step with `setHistoryDepth`, which publishes without a commit."*

Do not repair the grey in `button/Base.scss`. The inheriting `color` at the root is deliberate and is what lets the child glyph and text nodes own themed colours; the consumer supplying them is the contract, not a workaround.

Do not certify the badge from `createTopologyBar()`'s return value. It is a config object — `toolbar.Base` materialises `actions` into buttons with a spacer, and a formatter called off the declaration exercises the arithmetic and none of the wiring. This is the exact shape that shipped the #18551 regression past two reviews.

Do not check the arithmetic against a hand-published cursor. A formula tested against numbers the test invented can only confirm the model it was written from; drive real writes and cursor moves so `historyCursor` and `historyLength` are the engine's.
